translationRepairs: The Zhao king then moved north with Zhang Er and Chen Yu to secure territory on Yan's frontier.
The Zhao king then moved north with Chen Yu to secure territory on Yan's frontier.
Source has 與陳、餘, naming Chen Yu only; the original English invents Zhang Er, and the proposed idiomatic correctly removes him.
The Zhao king then moved north with Zhang Er and Chen Yu to secure territory on Yan's frontier.
The Zhao king then moved north with Chen Yu to secure territory on Yan's frontier.
Removing Zhang Er is required because the Chinese has only 陳、餘, but 'Chen and Yu' wrongly splits one personal name into two people; render as Chen Yu.
He added that even a woman now refused proper respect to Li Liang and urged him to pursue and kill her."
The King of Zhao has always ranked below General Li Liang, yet now even this woman will not step down from her carriage for him. Pursue and kill her."
The original omits 趙王素出將軍下 and softens 不為將軍下車. This revision restores both points, names Li Liang where 'the general' would be unclear, and preserves the continuing direct quotation.
Six years later, Marquis of Xuanping Ao died again.
Six years later, Marquis of Xuanping Ao also died.
After 魯元太后薨, 敖復薨 marks Ao's death in turn, not a second death of Ao; 'also died' correctly renders 復 here.
Six years later, Marquis of Xuanping Ao died again.
Six years later, Marquis of Xuanping Ao then died.
復 is sequential after the dowager's death, not iterative of Ao's own death; 'then died' is an accurate literal fix for 復薨.
In Yuanshi 2 of Emperor Ping, when broken noble lines were revived, Ao's great-great-great-grandson Qingji was made Marquis of Xuanping with a thousand-household estate.
In Yuanshi 2 of Emperor Ping, when broken noble lines were revived, Ao's great-great-grandson Qingji was made Marquis of Xuanping with a thousand-household estate.
玄孫 is the fourth-generation descendant (great-great-grandson); the original 'great-great-great-grandson' overcounts by one generation.
In the second year of Emperor Ping's Yuanshi era, continuing a severed line, Ao's great-great-great-grandson Qingji was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xuanping with a fief of one thousand households.
In the second year of Emperor Ping's Yuanshi era, continuing a severed line, Ao's great-great-grandson Qingji was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xuanping with a fief of one thousand households.
The same 玄孫 kinship error appears in the literal field; great-great-grandson is the correct English equivalent.
He added that even a woman now refused proper respect to Li Liang and urged him to pursue and kill her."
Moreover, the King of Zhao has always ranked below the general. Now even a woman will not step down from her carriage for the general. Please pursue and kill her."
The literal field also omitted 趙王素出將軍下 and blurred the carriage slight; this restores the source's full statement within the continuing direct speech.
One officer said the whole realm was in revolt and the able should establish themselves first.
One officer said, "The realm is in revolt against Qin, and the able should establish themselves first.
The literal field omitted Qin and failed to open the quotation after the speech tag; this restores 叛秦 and aligns the two-sentence speech.
"One officer said the whole realm was in revolt and the able should establish themselves first.
One officer said, "The realm is rising against Qin, and the capable should establish themselves first.
The opening quotation belonged after 'said,' and the original omitted Qin; this restores the referent and corrects the quote span.
